PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; WC vials and WC balls; toluene process control reagent; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating; 2-3 g of milled powder sampled after every 5 h for phase-evolution study. The 10 h state is an intermediate milling stage (parent process: 5 h milling).

overall_structure.value: Powder milled for 10 h (intermediate milling stage). The powder is still a partially alloyed mixture of elemental Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C: the diffraction peak intensity of all elements decreases with milling time (low intensity elemental peaks vanish after 5 h, and Al intensity only diminishes after 15 h, indicating the highest alloying rate for Al, so Al is still largely present at 10 h). Alloying is in progress and the uniform solid solution (BCC + γ-brass type) is only formed after 25 h of milling; BCC and γ-brass type phase markers begin to appear and grow during milling. SEM shows bulky, irregular, coarse particles of widely varying size.

source.reason: Structural/morphological characterization of the 10 h milled powder state.

unmapped_findings: The 10 h milled powder (aliases '10 h', 'milled 10 h'; SEM label '10 h MM') is characterised in this work only by SEM powder morphology (Fig. 2a) and the particle-size-distribution histogram (~10 ± 2 µm, Fig. 2f). All other quantitative measurements reported in the paper (Rietveld phase/lattice/crystallite data in Tables 2 and 4, DTA/thermal stability, annealing XRD, SPS processing, microhardness 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa, elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa, compressive strength 2046 ± 160 MPa with ~19% ductility, EDS/EPMA/WDS and CALPHAD modelling) pertain to the 35 h milled and/or spark-plasma-sintered states, NOT to the 10 h milled powder, so they are not assigned to this sample.
